name: Plan a week of LinkedIn posts
when: The founder wants to know what to post this week, or wants a steady rhythm before a launch.
procedure: Ask who the posts are for and what the founder wants from them this month: customers, hires, investors or a launch.
Choose 3 pillars, e.g. conviction (a point of view), building in public (the real work), proof (customers and results).
Plan 3 to 5 posts on weekdays, Tuesday to Thursday mornings first in the audience's time zone, never two in one day, at most one about the product itself.
For each post write: day, pillar, shape, hook pattern, a one-line angle, and the story or number it needs from the founder.
Use a different hook pattern for each post, and aim each at a different reaction: comments, saves, reposts.
Add a daily line: 10 to 20 thoughtful comments on peers' posts, written with the "Comment on a LinkedIn post" skill and sent by hand.
pitfalls: A plan full of topics with no story behind them produces generic posts: every row names the material it needs.
Six or more posts a week compete with each other.
verify: The plan has 3 to 5 posts on different days, 3 pillars with none over 60% of posts, no hook repeated, at most one product post, and each row names the material to get from the founder.
